name: San Francisco Board of Supervisors records, 1906-2026
counting_rules: One row is one thing the Board dealt with.
topic is single-valued, so no row is counted twice — but the topics sum to the rows that carry one, not to every row.
Do not count rows whose record_type is not `decision` into subject figures — they are page furniture, index rows, or a bare vote whose description lives in another row.
Say which denominator you used: all rows, decisions only, or classified rows only. All three are legitimate and they differ.

columns.name: id
columns.what: stable key: volume and item number

columns.name: date
columns.what: month-day where the volume printed one

columns.name: heading
columns.what: the title the volume printed above the item

columns.name: text
columns.what: the line as printed, original spelling and scan errors kept

columns.name: streets
columns.what: the street names the record itself printed, | separated

columns.name: refers_to_decision_number
columns.what: for a bare vote outcome, the decision number it points at — the thread back to the row that describes what was voted on. Blank when the row cites several

columns.name: how_we_know_where
columns.what: how precisely the record said where it happened. Only the first four are precise enough to draw a dot; `street only` means the street is known and the spot is not.

columns.name: why_no_place
values: named a street we could not use

columns.name: block
columns.what: assessor block, when there is one

columns.name: amount_count
columns.what: how many. Take amounts[0] only when this is 1 — 6.2% of rows carry several and none of them is THE amount.

columns.name: plain_line
columns.what: OUR one-sentence reading of the record in plain English, 6-11 words, written from the item's full text — NOT the Board's wording. `text` is the Board's. Empty where the record states no event (page furniture, an index row).

columns.name: importance
columns.what: OURS, not the Board's: 0-100 for how much the record matters, read off the plain_line by a reader applying a written rubric. Reach picks the band and stage discounts it, so an adopted citywide rule outranks the same rule referred. It is a reading, not a measurement, and it is for sorting a year into an order worth scanning — not a claim that one act mattered more than another. Empty where the record has no written line to read.

columns.name: plain_line_caution
columns.what: why a written line is doubtful, | separated, blank when it is not. `invented` = a name or figure in the line could not be found in the record; `overstates` = the line states as done what the record only proposed; `damaged` = the words match only approximately because the SCAN is broken, not the line. Filter on this rather than trusting every row.

columns.name: classified_by
columns.what: `record` means a human read this row. `form` means a human read the sentence-shape it shares with others. `fund` means the subject came from the fund the money was appropriated OUT OF — "Sewer Fund, Bond Issue 1904", "Municipal Railway Construction Fund" — which is the City's own word for what the money was for, printed in the record. `title` means a human read the Clerk's own file title for it — the modern record carries one, and the WHOLE title is the key, because `Administrative Code` alone heads 1,477 records about rent control, surveillance policy, police equipment and the film commission. `near-duplicate` means it is the same sentence as a labelled row with different scan errors. `rule` means a pattern that agreed 90-100% with a human read. `purpose-clause` means two reads: the opening formula gave the action, and the subject came from the clause after it — "for the purpose of reconstructing the main sewer in Mission street". Every row carries one of the five; a row can still have an empty `topic`, which is a read row whose line does not say what it was about.
